stimuli.title: A school-subject list made for this test
stimuli.description: A fictional list with new names, written for this assessment and not copied from the book.

stimuli.title: A new note about subjects
stimuli.description: A short new passage written only for this assessment.
stimuli.text: Rana likes science. She says art is fun. Science is useful for her. History is difficult for her.

questions.prompt: What subject is matched with Rami?
questions.objectiveLabel: Identify school subjects in a new table.
questions.evidence: Rami’s row in the new list says Geography.

questions.prompt: What day is shown in Mina’s row?
questions.objectiveLabel: Read a day from an original table.

questions.prompt: Which adjective does Rana use for art?
questions.objectiveLabel: Match subject opinions with taught adjectives.
questions.evidence: The new note says art is fun.

questions.prompt: Which subject does Rana call useful?
questions.objectiveLabel: Find a stated reason in an original passage.
questions.evidence: The new note states that science is useful for Rana.

questions.prompt: Which subject does Rana find difficult?
questions.objectiveLabel: Identify a subject and opinion in a new passage.
questions.evidence: The new note says history is difficult for Rana.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form: “Music and art ___ fun for our class.”
questions.objectiveLabel: Choose the singular present form in a new school context.
questions.evidence: The plural subject joined by “and” takes “are”.

questions.prompt: Which adjective gives a positive opinion about a school subject?
questions.objectiveLabel: Select an adjective that fits a clear context.
questions.evidence: “Useful” expresses a positive value; “boring” and “difficult” do not.

questions.prompt: A learner says a film does not interest him. Which word best describes the film?
questions.objectiveLabel: Choose an adjective from a new situation.
questions.evidence: A boring thing is not interesting.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that is correct for a made-up learner named Mina.
questions.objectiveLabel: Apply the taught third-person present form in a new example.
questions.evidence: The third-person singular form takes -s: Mina likes geography after school.

questions.prompt: Rewrite with the missing word: “I ___ music because it is fun.”
questions.evidence: “I like …” is a taught preference frame.
accepted: I like music because it is fun.

questions.prompt: Complete the new sentence: “The art club ___ fun on Tuesdays.”
questions.objectiveLabel: Choose the singular present form in a new school context.
questions.evidence: “The art club” is singular, so the present form is “is”.

questions.prompt: Rami’s class note says he is strong in science. Complete: “Rami is good at ___.”
questions.objectiveLabel: Complete a taught ability sentence using one stated subject.
questions.evidence: The original note says Rami is strong in science; “good at” expresses ability.
